output_text:
What this platform can actually do with your sensor CSV — concrete, existing capabilities:

1. map_csv — takes your headers (machine_id, temperature, vibration, timestamp) plus a sample row and generates a native HoloScript composition that maps each column to a scene dimension (e.g. one object per machine_id, temperature → color ramp, vibration → oscillation amplitude). This is the direct CSV→scene bridge.
2. map_data — the schema-level version: if you later expose the readings as a typed feed instead of a file, the same mapping survives the upgrade.
3. convert_format / list_targets — once mapped, the composition compiles to any registered target (web 3D, VR headset, native 2D dashboard), so the same data view follows you across devices.
4. select_modality — picks the right output form per device (a phone gets a 2D board, a Quest gets the walkable floor view), so you don't hand-design per platform.

The 2 best next moves:
- Move 1: run map_csv with your four headers and one real row → inspect the generated composition → adjust the temperature color ramp bounds to your alarm thresholds. Tool: map_csv, then apply_code to load it into the editor.
- Move 2: compile the mapped composition for the two devices your floor staff actually use. Tool: select_modality with platforms ["web","quest3"], then convert_format to those targets.

Marked uncertain (do not rely without checking): live streaming ingest of the CSV as a continuously-updating feed — the mapping tools are solid for snapshots; whether your update cadence works end-to-end depends on your data source wiring, which I have not verified here.
